A1.justification: Both PDFs describe HG-Lane and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures and supplementary Sections A–C. Corresponding content can be matched despite layout changes, renumbering and caption errors.

before.justification: v1 reports original lane-detection experiments, pipeline ablations, generative-quality measurements, a 20-person evaluation and tests on collected real-world images.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including quantitative comparisons and supplementary visual examples.

M1.justification: Figure 2 and Eq. 12 revise the reported Stage-II iP2P input from the clean original latent z0 to noisy latent zt, alongside the Stage-I output. Section 3.1 also separates color and Canny thresholds previously specified as shared. The frozen two-stage architecture and category-dependent refinement remain.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same six-condition CULane-derived benchmark, collected real-world weather/lighting images, and supplementary examples from TuSimple, OpenLane and CurveLanes. Appendix C only standardizes and reorders dataset names.

E2.justification: The lane-detector configurations in Table 3 remain identical. Generative comparisons retain Stable Diffusion, PITI, CycleGAN and Flux.1, and suppression comparisons retain all six restoration methods. Shortening the baseline enumeration in prose does not remove evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: The splits, dataset-size controls, metrics, 12 training epochs, Euler/Karras sampling settings, real-world sample counts and 20-person study remain unchanged. The removed dataset-split table is replaced by equivalent prose, and the training budget remains stated in Section 4.5.

E4.justification: The same five mask/pipeline ablations are retained in v1 Table 4 and v2 Table 2. The ablation images, generation comparisons and supplementary real-world, suppression and other-dataset examples contain the same analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same human-score means and plus/minus quantities for 20 participants and retain the same multiple-seed sampling discussion. No repeated-run counts, uncertainty-estimation procedures or significance tests are added or revised.

E6.justification: The generation-quality table corrects misplaced entries. PITI's F1@50/FID changes from 390.5/58.50 in v1 Table 5 to 58.50/390.5 in v2 Table 4. HG-Lane's F1@50/FID/CLIP-T changes from 80.1/0.23/88.49 to 88.49/80.1/0.23. These are reporting corrections, not demonstrated performance gains; the other result tables match.

T1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.3 revise the formal specification: the shared-threshold assumption is removed, and Stage-II's mathematical definition changes its latent arguments and explicitly defines noise prediction followed by iterative denoising. No theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: generation without re-annotation or fine-tuning, preservation of lane semantics, a 30,000-image benchmark and improved detection under adverse conditions. The headline improvement claims remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 4.9 newly explains the reported zero additional inference time through offline generation. The ablation interpretations, generalization arguments and limitation concerning location bias remain substantively unchanged.

D1.justification: Section 3.1 newly explains that annotation maps are constructed by filling original lane labels to a width covering the lane-line area, although the width remains unspecified. Hardware, software, sampling parameters and code/data access information are retained.

R1.justification: Both versions cite the same 45 works and retain the same research positioning. Updates such as publication details for references 7 and 25 concern the same cited works rather than new literature.

P1.justification: v2 corrects grammar and terminology, removes repetitive introductory and baseline prose, and replaces the dataset-split table with a concise description. Contact details, acknowledgments and bibliographic metadata are updated; the section structure remains.

P2.justification: Figure 2 revises arrows and latent labels, several tables and Figure 3 move, and the dataset-split table is removed with its information retained in prose. Supplementary Figures 6 and 7 exchange visual contents and positions, but their captions incorrectly describe the opposite comparison in v2.

improvement.justification: Correcting the misassigned metrics in v1 Table 5/v2 Table 4 resolves misleading comparisons and aligns HG-Lane's F1@50 with the other tables. Added mask-construction detail and copyediting provide modest further benefits. The newly mismatched appendix captions detract from clarity, but the numerical corrections support a limited net improvement without adding experimental validation.
